Tests assert stale rejection, deferred application, exact native calls and concrete user confirmation; no real configuration files are written. S3 actual native dynamic-tool schemas are compiled with array required members, including the previously null empty required list. Browser confirmation and actual native key-version tests remain distinct. Cycle2 NATIVE-CONFIG now asserts recorded config/batchWrite parameters: exact file, expected version, one model-key replace edit and reload=false, plus stale layer rejection. This establishes scoped native RPC intent and avoids claiming real native editor/file execution from a fake provider. Cycle3 native proposal regression distinguishes known startup failure before any batchWrite from ambiguous batchWrite failure. After restart, known prewrite absence remains confirmed and applies once; uncertain attempted write never replays. Cycle4 actual SQLite-trigger binding-write failure rolls back settings, applied proposal marker and all bindings together while retaining the existing native client; restart applies item/configuration/priority bindings. Independent native proposals from distinct project layers both write once, reread current session identities and keep old epochs retired despite delayed disconnect callbacks. Cycle5 confirmed configuration remains deferred while a compact running session exists, across3ticks and15held/14due-paused/1running sessions with undecodable histories. Runtime summary guards avoid loading those retained queues. Current incremental review: Retain the subject-specific assertions documented above for flow-configure-work.
